newsitem.title: USA: Atlanta cab driver arrested for making bombs.
newsitem.headline: Atlanta cab driver arrested for making bombs.

text.p: A 40-year-old cab driver was arrested and charged with making pipe bombs found in a vacant office outside Atlanta, police said on Friday.
But William Dennis Parham, described as a loner and a transient, was not believed to be connected with the Jan. 16 double-bombing that left six people injured at an Atlanta abortion clinic.

In fact, police said investigators did not believe the suspect was involved in any bombings, including the July 27 Centennial Olympic Park blast that left two people dead and more than 100 injured in downtown Atlanta at the height of the Summer Games.

Federal agents said four pipe bombs and a cache of bomb- making material were discovered by accident last weekend at a small roadside office building in the Dekalb County community known as Lithonia. Lithonia is located about 20 miles from the offices of the Atlanta Northside Family Planning Services centre in a suburb called Sandy Springs.
Parham was arrested on Thursday and charged with violating a Georgia state law against the manufacture of explosive devices. He did not face any alleged federal violations.
"Our people don't believe he was involved with any other bombings," said DeKalb County Police spokesman Chuck Johnson.

The Atlanta Journal-Constitution said Parham was living in the Lithonia office with his pet cat when a janitor found pipe bombs equipped with live fuses and wrapped with shotgun shells while cleaning up last Saturday.
The newspaper also quoted a friend of Parham's as saying the pipe bombs were at least two years old.
Meanwhile, agents from the FBI and U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms (ATF) continued their search for those responsible for the Jan. 16 abortion clinic bombing.

Officials said agents were canvassing hardware stores in the Atlanta area in hopes of tracing the source of nails used as shrapnel in the second of two bombs, which exploded as rescue workers swarmed the site.
Investigators also were revisiting explosives theft cases from across the country.
